text.p: Australian financial services group Colonial Ltd on Thursday said it aimed to bring its banking cost-to-income ratio down to around 55 percent.

Managing director Peter Smedley said Colonial State Bank's cost-to-income fell to 66.4 percent in the half-year ended June 30 from 74.1 percent a year ago, but still was still well behind the market leader National Australia Bank Ltd.
"We have indicated that we wish to see that come down and I would be looking forward at a rate certainly around the mid 50s, as a target base over the next couple of years," he said.
"And as a target base even in today's (tight) margin environment."
Smedley was speaking to reporters after the group reported a half-year net profit of A$118 million. Colonial State Bank accounted for almost half of the group's earnings.
It was Colonial's first profit announcement since it listed on the Australian stock market in May. Colonial offered no comparable profit for the same period a year ago.
Smedley said he did not have a target cost-to-income for the whole group, which fell to 50.4 percent from 58.9 percent in the half-year, but each business was improving its efficiency.
"The cost-to-income ratios for all businesses are down," Smedley said.
"It has been delivered in a wholesome way in a full attack on the cost base," he added.
Smedley called the cost-to-income ratio a benchmark measure of performance.
